newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cosmonauts quell blaze aboard Russia's Mir station.
newsitem.headline: Cosmonauts quell blaze aboard Russia's Mir station.

text.p: A fire broke out aboard Russia's orbiting Mir space station when cosmonauts tried to change an air filter, but the blaze was extinguished quickly and nobody was hurt, the head of the Russian Space Agency said on Monday.
Yuri Koptev said the fire broke out on Sunday night.
An official with Russia's military space forces said the blaze was "not a serious incident" and that it had been extinguished in seven minutes.
"There was no need to evacuate the Mir crew," he said.
It was the latest in a series of minor mishaps aboard Mir, which was launched in 1985 and which has already outlasted its expected lifespan.
Toilet tanks overflowed last year after delays in bringing supplies to the station and a new generator was hastily flown to the station after problems with energy supplies.
Six cosmonauts -- four Russians, one American and one German -- are currently aboard Mir.
